when: I consider using AI for a recurring task
do: try a representative, permitted example and compare the result with what the task actually requires
insteadOf: infer capability from a demonstration or a general benchmark
why: Capabilities vary between tasks. A local test gives you evidence for a specific use rather than a general impression.

when: a newer model or a materially different setup becomes available
do: rerun a task that previously failed and compare it with the earlier attempt
insteadOf: assume an old limitation still holds
why: A recorded failure can become a useful benchmark as models and tools change.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

when: an AI answer supplies a claim I intend to rely on
do: open the underlying source and check the claim, its context and any important limitations
insteadOf: treat a plausible citation or summary as sufficient evidence
why: A real source can still be interpreted poorly. Discovery and verification are separate jobs.

when: a conversation repeatedly defends the same mistaken premise
do: start a fresh conversation with the necessary facts and a neutral description of the problem
insteadOf: keep arguing inside the accumulated mistaken context
why: Earlier responses shape later ones. A fresh context can help escape an unproductive direction.

when: I ask AI for feedback on a proposal I favor
do: request concrete weaknesses, missing evidence and conditions under which it would fail
insteadOf: accept general encouragement as a quality judgment
why: Giving a critic a specific job can improve the feedback, although it does not remove sycophancy or make the feedback true.

when: I ask AI to produce something for an actual audience
do: state the goal, audience, relevant facts, constraints and the result I need
insteadOf: request a generic document and expect the AI to infer my situation
why: Context reduces the need for the model to invent a plausible setting for your request.

when: I delegate a multistep assignment to an agent
do: specify the intended result, permitted scope, required deliverables and the checks that establish completion
insteadOf: assign a broad goal without defining what an acceptable result looks like
why: Clear delegation makes execution and subsequent evaluation more useful.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

when: I decide whether repeated delegation is worthwhile
do: compare doing the task myself with the time for instructions, evaluation, repairs and unsuccessful attempts
insteadOf: count only how quickly the AI generated an answer
why: The time you spend checking can outweigh the apparent speed of production.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

when: an agent returns a completed assignment
do: evaluate the actual deliverables against the brief before using them
insteadOf: accept the agent’s report that the work is finished
why: Delegated execution moves your effort toward specification and evaluation; it does not remove responsibility for judging the result.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

when: an AI attempt misses the requirement
do: identify a concrete cause, improve the instructions or context, and stop if focused attempts keep failing
insteadOf: repeat the same vague request without learning from the result
why: Purposeful iterations help distinguish a fixable setup problem from a current capability limit.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

when: a revised approach solves a previously difficult AI task
do: save a short account of the working method for future attempts
insteadOf: reconstruct the successful approach from memory each time
why: A reusable description of a successful technique can help later agents handle the same difficulty.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

when: AI builds an artifact with behavior I can test
do: define checks of the requested behavior and use the observed failures to guide revisions
insteadOf: judge completion from a polished explanation or appearance alone
why: External feedback can support correction. The checks need to represent the actual goal, not just an easy proxy.

when: I need to choose an approach and have too few possibilities
do: ask for varied alternatives, challenge repetitive ones and select using my own criteria
insteadOf: commit to the first fluent suggestion
why: More possibilities help only when they contain meaningful variation and you exercise judgment in selecting among them.

source.section: When You Need Quantity to Find Quality

when: a minor obstruction interrupts work whose direction I already understand
do: ask for a few possible next moves and use them to resume my own work
insteadOf: abandon the task or hand over the whole piece automatically
why: A small intervention can restore progress while leaving the important thinking with you.

source.section: When You Need to Keep Moving

when: I need to adapt material I know for a new audience or format
do: provide the source and audience, then compare the result for missing caveats and altered meaning
insteadOf: assume a readable transformation preserved the substance
why: Knowing the material can make review efficient, but AI can smooth away qualifications that matter.

source.section: When You Need to Transform What You Already Have

when: I need to stress-test an interpretation or proposal
do: ask for distinct perspectives or a second analysis and investigate material disagreements
insteadOf: treat either agreement or a simulated persona as proof
why: Alternative perspectives can reveal omissions. They remain inputs, and several systems may share the same error.

source.section: When You Need a Different Perspective

when: I use AI while learning a method I need to perform myself
do: request hints and questions that leave me to attempt the next step, then explain my reasoning
insteadOf: read a complete solution and mistake its clarity for my understanding
why: Well-directed tutoring can support the effort needed to learn instead of bypassing it.

when: AI has begun doing a skill I want to retain
do: do some of that work myself or explain and reconstruct the method without relying on the answer
insteadOf: let successful assisted output stand in for my own capability
why: Unused abilities can decline. Intentional practice or a different pattern of assistance can preserve them.

when: I need a judgment or piece of writing to express my own considered view
do: record my initial reasoning before asking AI for criticism and alternatives
insteadOf: let its first answer silently become my own starting position
why: This companion exercise extends the book’s discussion of authorship and influence; it is an option for preserving an independent starting point.

source.section: How I Used AI to Write This Book

when: the effort or care I put into a task matters to another person
do: decide which contribution I should make personally and fit any assistance around it
insteadOf: optimize the wording or speed without considering what the work communicates
why: Some work carries meaning through who did it and why. That expectation depends on the relationship and circumstances.

when: AI helps with work in a field I need to understand well
do: continue studying the underlying facts and work through examples that build my own judgment
insteadOf: assume access to fluent answers removes the need for expertise
why: Internal knowledge helps you ask sharper questions and recognize where an answer fails.

when: a familiar approach gives me little traction on a problem
do: draw on a framework from another field, ask AI to apply it, and assess whether the connection is useful
insteadOf: keep asking for more versions of the same approach
why: Breadth gives you ways to direct an AI beyond its default response. An analogy still needs to fit the problem.

when: I review work in a field whose quality matters to me
do: compare strong and weak human examples and explain what I value or reject
insteadOf: use average AI output as my only standard
why: Exposure and considered reactions build the judgment needed to select useful material from abundant output.

when: AI makes one step much faster but the final outcome barely changes
do: trace the handoffs and identify the next constraint before generating more output
insteadOf: assume additional speed at my step will fix the whole process
why: A bottleneck can move. Improvements need to reach the outcome rather than accumulate as extra work waiting for someone else.

source.section: O-Rings, Garbage Cans, and Dissolving Walls

when: I ask a team to share useful AI experiments
do: make permitted experimentation clear and commit to concrete benefits for the people sharing improvements
insteadOf: request openness while leaving punishment, replacement or workload expectations unresolved
why: People may rationally hide gains when disclosure threatens them. Credible commitments matter more than enthusiasm.

when: automation removes work that previously taught a junior colleague
do: create a learning assignment with meaningful challenge, wider context and feedback from an experienced person
insteadOf: remove the task without replacing its learning function
why: Short-term efficiency can weaken the future supply of expertise if novices lose the experiences that build it.

when: an AI recommendation seems unusually tailored or convincing
do: check its factual support and ask whose objective and incentives the advice advances
insteadOf: equate personal relevance or friendliness with trustworthy evidence
why: The ability to tailor an argument can serve understanding, sales or deception. Persuasiveness does not distinguish among them.

when: a recording or apparent message asks me to take a consequential action
do: confirm the source through an independent, established route before acting
insteadOf: rely on a convincing voice or image as sufficient proof
why: Synthetic media make impersonation easier. This generalizes the book’s advice to establish identity beyond a suspicious interaction.

when: working with agents expands how much work I can initiate
do: set a limit on concurrent assignments and a stopping point I can sustain
insteadOf: let additional capacity turn every spare moment into another task to supervise
why: Greater production capacity can intensify work and overwhelm attention unless you set boundaries.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

when: I consider automating a task that feels repetitive or ceremonial
do: check whether it still supports a real decision, relationship or obligation before delegating it
insteadOf: assume that an irritating process has no meaningful purpose
why: Routine work may be dispensable ritual, but it can also carry important human value. The distinction matters before automation.
